chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Pray the prescribed prayers, then enter into Ihram for Hajj or for Umrat al-Tamattu', and go out without Talbiyah until you ascend to the beginning of Al-Bayda', to the first mile on your left. So when the ground becomes level for you, whether you are riding or walking, then say Talbiah. It will not harm you whether you enter Ihram at night or during the day. And the Masjid of Dhu al-Hulayfa is that which was outside the pavilions, from the courtyard of the Masjid. Then today, there is nothing of the pavilions remaining from it.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram: The sacred state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.السَّقَائِف: Al-Saqā'if: The pavilions or covered structures surrounding the mosque
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاء: Al-Bayda': A plain near Mecca, traditionally the starting point for Ihram
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: Talbiyah: The ritual invocation 'Labbayk' recited during Hajj
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Masjid Dhu al-Hulayfa: The specific mosque near Mecca designated as the Miqat

ai.seo_question: When and where should a pilgrim recite the Talbiah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual protocol for entering Ihram, emphasizing the sequence of performing the obligatory prayer before assuming the state of consecration. It provides precise geographical markers for the Miqat at Al-Bayda' and clarifies the historical location of Masjid Dhu al-Hulayfa, reflecting the scholarly attention to physical landmarks in Shia jurisprudence. The instruction to delay the Talbiah until the ground levels out highlights the importance of intentionality and proper timing in the pilgrimage rites.
